chunks.title: Blocking public access to your Amazon S3 storage
chunks.topic: S3 Block Public Access scope and behavior
chunks.summary: Amazon S3 Block Public Access has four independent settings that can be applied at bucket, account, access-point, and organization levels. AWS combines applicable settings using the most restrictive effective controls; bucket-only values do not describe the complete account-level access decision.

chunks.title: Protecting data with server-side encryption
chunks.summary: Amazon S3 server-side encryption is applied as objects are written. AWS documents SSE-S3 as the baseline encryption for new object uploads, while bucket default-encryption settings describe the encryption configuration applied to new uploads. A bucket-level setting is not an inventory of historical object encryption.

chunks.title: Security group rules
chunks.summary: Security group rules allow inbound or outbound traffic and specify protocol, port, and source or destination. When multiple security groups are associated with a resource, their rules are aggregated, so reviewing one group's ingress alone does not establish effective reachability.

chunks.title: Policies and permissions in AWS Identity and Access Management
chunks.summary: AWS IAM supports several policy types, including identity-based, resource-based, permissions-boundary, session, and organization policies. Policies are evaluated when a principal makes a request, so one policy document by itself is not a complete effective-permissions or exploitability assessment.

chunks.title: Security best practices in AWS CloudTrail
chunks.summary: AWS recommends creating a CloudTrail trail for an ongoing event record and describes multi-Region trails as a way to capture activity across enabled Regions. CloudTrail's event history and trails have different coverage and retention characteristics, so a simplified trail-field check does not establish the state of all logging in an organization.
